as_told.title: Proposed project to clean the shafts with robots, with the University of Ferrara

plain: Filippo Biondi is a researcher who says he has used scanning to look beneath the pyramids at Giza, in Egypt. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels in late 2025, he spoke of the Khafre Research Project, named after Khafre, one of the great Giza pyramids, and said it might become the center of the work. He names fellow researchers Armando Mei and Corrado Malanga, and the University of Ferrara, a university in Italy. Speaking again on the same show in March 2026, he says the team is still preparing a proposal to send to the Egyptian government. In that telling the focus is on clearing shafts under the pyramid that are filled with debris, and he says robots would do the cleaning. He adds that the proposal, involving the University of Ferrara, would go in within weeks. If it went ahead, he says, it could open up what lies below the pyramid. All the tellings come from Biondi himself, across two episodes, and they differ mainly on how far along the proposal is.
